images.filename: Greedy Gut from Chalk Bank - geograph.org.uk - 307781.jpg
images.caption: Greedy Gut from Chalk Bank, Spurn, East Riding of Yorkshire, England.Greedy Gut, seen here at low tide in January. Greedy Gut is a channel of water just slightly deeper than the mudflats surrounding it leading to a stony bank off Spurn peninsula known as Old Den. Here, just off Chalk Bank on the north-west side of Spurn, the ground is only broken up by erosion during tidal surges combined with strong westerly winds. At all other times sand and silt is deposited here from erosion on the seaward side.
images.alt: Greedy Gut from Chalk Bank, Spurn, East Riding of Yorkshire, England.Greedy Gut, seen here at low tide in January. images.caption: Don't Spurn Spurn, East Riding of Yorkshire, England! It would seem this ever dynamic sand spit is reaching the end of its 250 year life cycle! images.caption: Road to Spurn Head, East Riding of Yorkshire, England.Maintaining the road to Spurn Head is a challenge in this constantly changing and storm-affected environment. This stretch, with its rough block surface, is almost engulfed in sand requiring some care by motorists. The Yorkshire Wildlife Trust charges a toll, currently £3, to drive the three miles to Spurn Head.
